hero.title: Which one of us? The secret vote game
hero.description: You each vote on your own, both answers are revealed at once… and you find out how alike you really see things.

section1.title: A silly little game, and yet
section1.p1: You already know the idea. One question, two possible answers, one truth: you, or the other one. Except that at a party, whoever shouts loudest is always right… Here, nobody can talk over anybody. You each vote on your own, in secret, and both answers land at the same time.
section1.p2: It's silly. It works every single time.
section1.p3: What makes the game funny isn't the rounds where you agree. It's the other ones. The ones where you look up and go “hang on, you honestly think I'm the one who complains most in traffic?”
section1.p4: Twelve rounds, four minutes flat, a harmony score at the end. And one phone, that's it.

section2.title: How you play
section2.intro: Nothing complicated, but the four points below make all the difference.
section2.etape1Texte: The game uses them everywhere: on the buttons, in the reveal, in the final score. Far more alive than “player 1” and “player 2”.
section2.etape2Titre: The first one votes in secret
section2.etape2Texte: The question appears and you pick which one of you it describes best. The other one mustn't look… that's the whole point!
section2.etape3Texte: The game asks you to, out loud. The second player votes without knowing what the first one chose.
section2.etape4Texte: A countdown, then both cards flip at once. Same answer: a point. Different answers: a debate.
section2.apres: At the end you get a harmony percentage, your best run of agreements in a row, and the list of questions you disagreed on. That list, honestly, is the best part of the game.

section3.title: The four families of questions
section3.intro: Forty questions in total, split across four themes. Each game draws twelve of them, evenly spread: no chance of landing twelve questions about the washing-up.
section3.apres: Start another game and the twelve questions change. Plenty of reason to come back without going in circles.

themes.quotidien: “…always forgets to buy the one thing you needed?”

section4.title: Why it works so well as a couple
section4.p1: There's one thing couple tests never do: put you face to face with the picture your partner has of you. A test hands you a result. Here, you find out your other half sees you as the most stubborn one of the pair… and you're going to have to talk about it!
section4.p2: That's usually when the evening really starts.
section4.p3: And no, a low score doesn't mean things are going badly. It mostly means you've never asked each other these questions out loud. Couples who score 100 % aren't necessarily the happiest, either: sometimes they've simply been telling themselves the same story for ten years.

faq.title: Questions we get asked
faq.q1: How many people do you need?
faq.a1: Two, and one phone. The game is built around passing the screen back and forth, not playing from separate devices.
faq.q2: How long does a game last?
faq.a2: Four to five minutes for the twelve rounds… if you don't stop to argue at every disagreement. Which happens a lot.
faq.q3: Is it free? Do I need an account?
faq.a3: Free, and no sign-up. Open the page, type your first names, play. Nothing is stored.
faq.q4: Can we play more than once?
faq.a4: Yes. The twelve rounds are drawn at random from forty questions, so two games in a row never look alike.
faq.q5: What if we agree on nothing?
faq.a5: That's the best case, genuinely. The game hands you the list of contested questions at the end, and it's exactly the kind of conversation nobody ever starts on their own.
faq.q6: Does it work for a brand new couple?
faq.a6: Yes, but expect a low score and a lot of laughing. The questions in the laughs theme land beautifully early on, the ones about the future rather less so.

section5.title: Fancy carrying on?
section5.p1: If the secret vote idea worked for you, the rest of our games run on the same principle: getting you talking without making it obvious.
